title: Asbestos scope, definitions, classes of work and exposure limits practice questions
description: Practice questions on OSHA's construction asbestos rule: scope, ACM and PACM, Class I-IV work, key terms, exposure and multi-employer duties.

questions.question: A crew on a construction site is applying an asbestos-containing asphalt roof coating. What does 1926.1101(a)(8) say about this material?

options.A: It is Class II asbestos work
options.B: The section does not apply to asbestos-containing asphalt roof coatings
options.C: It must be treated as PACM
options.D: It is covered only if the coating is friable

questions.explanation: Paragraph (a)(8) states: "This section does not apply to asbestos-containing asphalt roof coatings, cements and mastics."

questions.question: Under 1926.1101(a)(7), what is coverage under the asbestos standard based on?

options.A: The employer's industry classification code
options.B: The number of employees on the site
options.C: The dollar value of the construction contract
options.D: The nature of the work operation involving asbestos exposure

questions.explanation: Paragraph (a)(7) states: "Coverage under this standard shall be based on the nature of the work operation involving asbestos exposure."

questions.question: A product contains chrysotile that was chemically treated during manufacture. Under the 1926.1101(b) definition of asbestos, how is this mineral treated?

options.A: It is asbestos, because the definition includes any of the listed minerals that has been chemically treated and/or altered
options.B: It is no longer asbestos once chemical treatment has changed it
options.C: It is asbestos only while it remains friable
options.D: It is asbestos only in buildings constructed no later than 1980

questions.explanation: The definition lists chrysotile and the other minerals and adds "any of these minerals that has been chemically treated and/or altered."

questions.question: Employees will disturb PACM that has never been sampled. For purposes of 1926.1101, does the term "asbestos" cover this material?

options.A: No, it is covered only after a laboratory confirms more than one percent asbestos
options.B: Only if the PACM is friable
options.C: Yes, because for purposes of the standard "asbestos" includes PACM
options.D: No, PACM is covered only by EPA's school asbestos rule

questions.explanation: The definition of asbestos ends: "For purposes of this standard, “asbestos” includes PACM, as defined below."

questions.question: Sprayed-on acoustical plaster in a building constructed in 1972 is PACM under 1926.1101(b). What does the definition say about that designation?

options.A: It can never be removed for the life of the building
options.B: It may be rebutted pursuant to paragraph (k)(5)
options.C: It lapses automatically three years after the building's last inspection
options.D: It applies only while the plaster is damaged

questions.explanation: PACM is thermal system insulation and surfacing material in buildings constructed no later than 1980, and "The designation of a material as “PACM” may be rebutted pursuant to paragraph (k)(5) of this section."

questions.question: Under the 1926.1101(b) definitions, what separates Class I asbestos work from Class II asbestos work?

options.A: Whether the material is friable or nonfriable
options.B: The quantity of material removed in one day
options.C: Whether the work is done indoors or outdoors
options.D: Whether the material removed is thermal system insulation or surfacing material

questions.explanation: Class I is "the removal of TSI and surfacing ACM and PACM", while Class II is "the removal of ACM which is not thermal system insulation or surfacing material."

questions.question: Both Class III and Class IV work can involve maintenance. Under 1926.1101(b), what marks the maintenance and custodial activities that are Class IV work?

options.A: Only nonfriable material is present in the work area
options.B: The task takes less than one hour
options.C: Employees contact but do not disturb ACM or PACM
options.D: No PACM is present anywhere in the building

questions.explanation: Class IV work "means maintenance and custodial activities during which employees contact but do not disturb ACM or PACM". Class III covers repair and maintenance operations where ACM "is likely to be disturbed."

questions.question: A crew will remove thermal system insulation in a 1975 building. The insulation is PACM and has never been sampled. How does the 1926.1101(b) definition of Class I work apply?

options.A: Class I covers the removal of TSI and surfacing ACM and PACM, so this removal is Class I work
options.B: It becomes Class I work only after sampling shows more than one percent asbestos
options.C: It is Class II work, because the material is presumed rather than confirmed
options.D: It is Class IV work until the material is sampled

questions.explanation: "Class I asbestos work means activities involving the removal of TSI and surfacing ACM and PACM."

questions.topic: Work terms: disturbance, removal and repair
questions.question: A maintenance task on ACM does not crumble or pulverize it, but it does generate visible debris from the material. Under 1926.1101(b), is this a disturbance?

options.A: No, a disturbance requires the matrix to be pulverized
options.B: No, unless the debris fills more than one glove bag
options.C: Only if the ACM is thermal system insulation
options.D: Yes, disturbance includes activities that generate visible debris from ACM or PACM

questions.explanation: "Disturbance means activities that disrupt the matrix of ACM or PACM, crumble or pulverize ACM or PACM, or generate visible debris from ACM or PACM."

questions.topic: Work terms: disturbance, removal and repair
questions.question: Under 1926.1101(b), encapsulation of ACM attached to a structure falls within which defined term?

options.A: Repair
options.B: Removal
options.C: Demolition
options.D: Aggressive method

questions.explanation: Repair means overhauling, rebuilding, reconstructing, or reconditioning of structures or substrates, "including encapsulation or other repair of ACM or PACM attached to structures or substrates."

questions.question: Under 1926.1101(b), a regulated area covers the area where Class I, II, and III asbestos work is conducted and what other area?

options.A: Every room on the same floor of the building
options.B: Any area within 25 feet of the work
options.C: Any adjoining area where debris and waste from such asbestos work accumulate
options.D: Any area where Class IV work is conducted

questions.explanation: A regulated area is "an area established by the employer to demarcate areas where Class I, II, and III asbestos work is conducted, and any adjoining area where debris and waste from such asbestos work accumulate".

questions.question: A contractor seals plastic over all openings into a work area as a critical barrier. Under 1926.1101(b), what must a critical barrier be sufficient to do?

options.A: Keep the work area under negative pressure
options.B: Prevent airborne asbestos in a work area from migrating to an adjacent area
options.C: Hold all of the waste generated by the job
options.D: Trap at least 99.97 percent of particles 0.3 micrometers in diameter

questions.explanation: "Critical barrier means one or more layers of plastic sealed over all openings into a work area or any other similarly placed physical barrier sufficient to prevent airborne asbestos in a work area from migrating to an adjacent area."

questions.question: One of the employer's own carpenters wants to step into a regulated area to watch the removal, although nothing in his work duties requires him to be there. Under 1926.1101(b), what makes a person an "authorized person"?

options.A: Wearing a respirator while inside the regulated area
options.B: Being escorted by a member of the abatement crew
options.C: Having passed a respirator fit test
options.D: Being authorized by the employer and required by work duties to be present in regulated areas

questions.explanation: The definition has two parts: "Authorized person means any person authorized by the employer and required by work duties to be present in regulated areas."

questions.question: A company leases a building and controls its management and record keeping functions. Which description of "building/facility owner" in 1926.1101(b) fits this company?

options.A: The legal entity, including a lessee, which exercises control over management and record keeping functions
options.B: Only the holder of the recorded deed to the property
options.C: The general contractor on any project in the building
options.D: The competent person assigned to the building

questions.explanation: The rule says "Building/facility owner is the legal entity, including a lessee, which exercises control over management and record keeping functions relating to a building and/or facility" in which activities covered by the standard take place.

questions.question: Under 1926.1101(b), when do historic workplace conditions "closely resemble" the conditions of the current workplace?

options.A: When the historic job was done by the same employees in the same building
options.B: When the major workplace conditions which contributed to the levels of historic asbestos exposure are no more protective than conditions of the current workplace
options.C: When the historic workplace conditions were more protective than those of the current workplace
options.D: When the historic job took place within the past 30 days

questions.explanation: "Closely resemble means that the major workplace conditions which have contributed to the levels of historic asbestos exposure, are no more protective than conditions of the current workplace."

questions.question: Under 1926.1101(b), what does a negative initial exposure assessment demonstrate?

options.A: That no asbestos is present in the building
options.B: That one past air sample was below the PELs
options.C: That employee exposure during an operation is expected to be consistently below the PELs
options.D: That all employees in the area wear respirators

questions.explanation: It is "a demonstration by the employer, which complies with the criteria in paragraph (f)(2)(iii) of this section, that employee exposure during an operation is expected to be consistently below the PELs."

questions.question: On a multi-employer worksite, an enclosure containing Class I work has a significant breach. Under the example in 1926.1101(d)(2), what shall happen?

options.A: The building/facility owner shall repair the breach within 24 hours
options.B: The general contractor shall repair the breach at the end of the shift
options.C: Each employer whose employees are nearby shall repair its share of the breach
options.D: The employer responsible for erecting the enclosure shall repair the breach immediately

questions.explanation: Paragraph (d)(2) says hazards "shall be abated by the contractor who created or controls the source of asbestos contamination" and gives the example: "if there is a significant breach of an enclosure containing Class I work, the employer responsible for erecting the enclosure shall repair the breach immediately."

questions.question: Employees working immediately adjacent to a Class I job are exposed to asbestos because the job's containment is inadequate. Under the example in 1926.1101(d)(3), which is one of the options their employer shall take?

options.A: Remove the employees from the area until the enclosure breach is repaired
options.B: Have its own employees repair the other contractor's enclosure
options.C: Keep working until the next daily check of the enclosure
options.D: Leave all action to the primary asbestos contractor

questions.explanation: Their employer "shall either remove the employees from the area until the enclosure breach is repaired; or perform an initial exposure assessment pursuant to (f) of this section."

questions.question: Under 1926.1101(d)(4), what must employers of employees working adjacent to another employer's regulated area take steps on a daily basis to ascertain?

options.A: The asbestos content of every material in the regulated area
options.B: The integrity of the enclosure and/or the effectiveness of the control method relied on by the primary asbestos contractor
options.C: The training records of the primary asbestos contractor's workers
options.D: The air monitoring results inside the regulated area

questions.explanation: They "shall take steps on a daily basis to ascertain the integrity of the enclosure and/or the effectiveness of the control method relied on by the primary asbestos contractor to assure that asbestos fibers do not migrate to such adjacent areas."

questions.question: The general contractor on a project that includes asbestos work is not qualified to serve as the asbestos competent person. Under 1926.1101(d)(5), what shall it do as supervisor of the entire project?

options.A: Serve as the competent person for all Class I work
options.B: Repair every enclosure breach on the site itself
options.C: Ascertain whether the asbestos contractor is in compliance and require it to come into compliance when necessary
options.D: Perform all air monitoring for the asbestos contractor

questions.explanation: "As supervisor of the entire project, the general contractor shall ascertain whether the asbestos contractor is in compliance with this standard, and shall require such contractor to come into compliance with this standard when necessary."
